---
title: "B · Footprints & PSF — results"
---

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
**Bottom line.** Simple spherical-Earth trigonometry reproduces real pixel sizes for all three
sensors (MODIS 1 → 4.8 × 2.0 km, VIIRS 0.78 → 1.6 km with its aggregation saw-tooth, ECOSTRESS
70 → 90 m). For areal means the pixel model matters in two situations: **small polygons** (a few
pixels; the centre-in-polygon rule is worst, and may find no pixel at all at a MODIS swath edge) and
**overlapping scans** (MODIS/VIIRS swath edges, ECOSTRESS scan overlap), where any scheme that lets
overlapping pixels *share* the ground — overlap-aware footprints, or simply **Voronoi cells, which need
no sensor model** — cuts the error by 30–40 %. Adding the instrument PSF does not improve polygon means on
average: it can only re-weight blurred observations, and a PSF-optimal (least-squares) weighting helps
only for the smallest MODIS polygons. For polygons ≥ 10 km at nadir, all reasonable choices agree to
within a few hundredths of a kelvin.
:::

## Pixel size vs. view angle

![](figures/footprint_size.png)

The spherical-Earth model (lines) matches the spacing of pixel centres in the geolocation files
(dots) for all three sensors, including the VIIRS saw-tooth caused by on-board aggregation (3:1 →
2:1 at 31.6°, 2:1 → 1:1 at 44.7°). Model sizes at the swath edge: MODIS 4.8 × 2.0 km
(from 1 × 1 km at nadir), VIIRS 1.6 × 1.6 km (from 0.78 × 0.74 km), ECOSTRESS ~90 × 86 m (from
71 × 77 m). ECOSTRESS centre spacing scatters more because its L1B geolocation is
terrain-corrected and its scans overlap.

## Pixels as vectors

![](figures/footprint_maps.png)

Every pixel near a target is exported as an oriented quadrilateral (trigonometric footprint) and
as its Voronoi cell, with view zenith, size, LST and all weights as attributes
(FlatGeobuf, [`results/vectors/`](https://github.com/ashiklom/simon-code-research/tree/main/l2-swath-geolocation/results/vectors); county-sized exports are produced by
`scripts/20_footprints.py` into `data/vectors/`). At nadir, footprints and Voronoi cells are
nearly the same squares. At the MODIS swath edge, footprints of consecutive scans overlap by
~50 % (the bow-tie), so each pixel can only claim about half its footprint; Voronoi cells instead
split the overlap into irregular slivers. VIIRS' bow-tie-deleted pixels (no data) are removed
before either construction.

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
viewof fpScene = Inputs.select(["modis_aqua_nadir", "modis_aqua_edge", "viirs_n20_nadir", "viirs_snpp_edge", "ecostress"], {value: "modis_aqua_edge", label: "scene"})
viewof fpPoly = Inputs.radio(["circle_10km", "box_3km"], {value: "box_3km", label: "polygon"})
viewof fpKind = Inputs.radio(["footprints", "voronoi"], {value: "footprints", label: "pixel shape"})
viewof fpColor = Inputs.select(["lst_K", "vza", "w_naive_center", "w_voronoi", "w_footprint_pou", "w_psf_pou"], {value: "lst_K", label: "colour by"})
fpData = {
  try { return await d3.json(`data/site/${fpScene}__${fpPoly}__${fpKind}.geojson`); }
  catch (e) { return {type: "FeatureCollection", features: []}; }
}
polysAll = FileAttachment("data/targets/polygons.geojson").json()
// d3-geo expects clockwise exterior rings (shapely/GeoJSON writes counter-clockwise): reverse them
rewind = f => ({...f, geometry: {...f.geometry, coordinates: f.geometry.type === "Polygon"
  ? f.geometry.coordinates.map(r => [...r].reverse())
  : f.geometry.coordinates.map(p => p.map(r => [...r].reverse()))}})
fpTarget = ({type: "FeatureCollection", features: polysAll.features.filter(f => f.properties.name === fpPoly).map(rewind)})
```

::: {.widget}
```{ojs}
//| echo: false
Plot.plot({width: 640, height: 520, projection: {type: "azimuthal-equal-area", rotate: d3.geoCentroid(fpTarget).map(v => -v),
                                                domain: fpData.features.length ? fpData : fpTarget, inset: 10},
  color: {type: "linear", scheme: "blues", legend: true, label: fpColor},
  marks: [Plot.geo(fpData, {fill: d => d.properties[fpColor], stroke: "#52514e", strokeWidth: 0.3, fillOpacity: 0.85,
                            title: d => `row ${d.properties.row}, col ${d.properties.col}\nVZA ${d.properties.vza}°\n${d.properties.W_s_m} × ${d.properties.W_t_m} m\nLST ${d.properties.lst_K} K`}),
          Plot.geo(fpTarget, {stroke: "#e34948", strokeWidth: 2, fill: "none"})]})
```
Hover a pixel for its geometry. Large ECOSTRESS subsets are not shipped to the browser.
:::

## Areal means of real LST

![](figures/areal_real.png)

Differences relative to the PSF-aware (overlap-aware) mean, for the three polygons in each scene:

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
areal = FileAttachment("data/site/areal_means.csv").csv({typed: true})
schemes = ["naive_center", "naive_square", "voronoi", "footprint", "footprint_pou", "psf", "psf_pou", "psf_lsq"]
Inputs.table(areal.map(d => Object.fromEntries([["scene", d.scene], ["polygon", d.polygon], ["VZA", d.vza_mean.toFixed(1)],
  ["centres in", d.n_center_in], ["pixels touching", d.n_touching],
  ...schemes.map(s => [s, d[`mean_${s}`] == null || isNaN(d[`mean_${s}`]) ? "–" : d[`mean_${s}`].toFixed(2)])])), {rows: 18})
```

With real LST, the choice changes polygon means by **up to 0.9 K for the 3 km square**
(centre-in-polygon on VIIRS and MODIS at nadir, where only ~8–16 centres fall inside), by **0.1–0.3 K**
for the square at swath edges or mid-swath, and by **< 0.1 K** for the 10 km circle and the county —
except that schemes which ignore scan overlap (centre, nominal square, plain footprint, plain PSF)
differ by 0.07–0.10 K for the county at the VIIRS swath edge and by 0.08–0.14 K for ECOSTRESS, whose
overlapping scans count part of the ground twice. At the MODIS swath edge, no pixel centre falls inside the
3 km square at all, so centre-in-polygon has no answer.

## Synthetic truth: which pixel model gets the polygon mean right?

![](figures/areal_synthetic.png)

Real LST has no ground truth, so the 70 m ECOSTRESS LST from the same afternoon served as a "true"
field: each MODIS/VIIRS pixel observed it through its real footprint and PSF, and each weighting
scheme estimated the mean of 200 random squares and circles (2, 5, 10, 20 km; 50 per size) in each scene.

* Errors fall with polygon size (2 km: 0.3–1.8 K; 20 km: 0.17–0.30 K) and are not bias (|mean error| ≤ 0.05 K):
  they are boundary effects — every edge pixel's value mixes inside and outside the polygon, which no
  weighting of blurred pixels can undo.
* **Near nadir** all schemes except centre-in-polygon are equivalent; centre-in-polygon is 30–40 % worse for 2 km polygons.
* **At swath edges**, overlap-aware schemes win clearly: VIIRS edge RMSE 0.28 vs 0.39 K (10 km) and
  0.17 vs 0.27 K (20 km); MODIS edge 0.20 vs 0.30 K (20 km). **Voronoi ≈ overlap-aware footprints.**
* PSF weights (overlap-aware) are no better than footprint weights on average; the NNLS "PSF-optimal"
  weights help for small MODIS polygons (2 km at nadir: 0.38 vs 0.49 K; 5 km at the edge: 0.70 vs 0.84 K)
  but not consistently elsewhere.

Caveats: the "truth" is itself a 70 m blurred measurement (finer structure is missing, so MODIS/VIIRS
errors are if anything underestimated); retrieval, time-of-day and geolocation errors are excluded on
purpose.

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
synth = FileAttachment("data/site/synthetic_errors.csv").csv({typed: true})
synthTable = {
  const out = [];
  for (const [scene, g1] of d3.group(synth, d => d.scene)) for (const [size, g2] of d3.group(g1, d => d.size_m)) {
    const row = {scene, "size km": size / 1000, n: g2.length};
    for (const s of schemes) { const v = g2.map(d => d[`err_${s}`]).filter(x => x != null && !isNaN(x)); row[s] = v.length ? Math.sqrt(d3.mean(v, x => x * x)).toFixed(2) : "–"; }
    out.push(row);
  }
  return out;
}
Inputs.table(synthTable, {rows: 20})
```
RMSE (K) of the polygon-mean LST over the random polygons, per scene and polygon size.
